articles.title: Red Bull narrowly defended after difficult new F1 chapter start
articles.body: Red Bull's first campaign as a bona fide engine manufacturer has been, by their own lofty standards, a humbling experience. Fourth in the constructors' standings with 177 points, zero wins, and a best result of second place for Max Verstappen in Austria and Hungary, the six-time constructors' champions have looked a shadow of the dominant force they were not so long ago. When we asked RacingNews365 readers whether Red Bull should be doing better this season, the response was almost perfectly split: 51.4% said no, while 48.6% said yes. It is a telling divide, one that captures the two sides of this debate neatly. Those in the 'no' camp have a reasonable argument. This is the first year Red Bull has raced with a fully in-house power unit, the Red Bull Ford DM01, following years of reliance on Honda hardware. Team principal Laurent Mekies warned before the season that expecting to match established engine manufacturers from day one "would be naive," and that there would be "a fair amount of struggles, headaches, sleepless nights." In that context, four podiums and a clear upward trajectory, Verstappen has been on the rostrum in four of the last seven grands prix, can be viewed as credible progress. Yet the 48% who want more have a point, too. This is still a team built around a four-time world champion, operating from one of the finest facilities in the sport, and sitting 202 points behind championship leaders Mercedes. Five DNFs across 11 races is a stark figure, and Verstappen himself has not minced words, describing the season as "very tough" and acknowledging that Red Bull "want to win" and "want to dominate," rather than simply collect the occasional podium. The truth, as the poll suggests, lies somewhere in between. The foundations of the manufacturer project are laid; the question is how quickly Red Bull can build upon them. articles.title: Virgin Trains granted track access for new Channel Tunnel routes from 2030
articles.body: Virgin Trains has been given track access for new services between London and Paris, Brussels and Amsterdam in 2030, in a step forward for its plans to rival Eurostar. Rail regulator the Office of Rail and Road (ORR) said it had granted approval for Sir Richard Branson’s company to run up to 20 new daily return services through the Channel Tunnel . The agreement covers the period between October 1 2030 to December 31 2040. It means Virgin Trains has passed another key regulatory hurdle towards starting the international services, after being granted access last October to share Eurostar’s Temple Mills depot in east London to maintain and store trains. Temple Mills is the only depot that can be accessed from High Speed 1, the line that runs between London and the tunnel. Eurostar has held a monopoly on passenger services through the tunnel since it opened in 1994. Sir Richard previously said it was “time to end this 30-year monopoly and bring some Virgin magic to the cross-Channel route”. It plans to run services between St Pancras and the same stations in Paris, Brussels and Amsterdam used by Eurostar. The ORR said the decision to grant track access was “an important next step”, but that there was “still more work to do” before the new services can run. Deputy director of access and international Martin Jones said: “This is an important next step in bringing competition and growth to the market for international rail services, and we welcome the progress Virgin Trains and London St Pancras High Speed have made. “While there is still more work to do, we are supporting Virgin and the wider industry to grow international services.” For example, Virgin Trains must secure access to other rail networks and obtain safety approvals from the ORR and relevant regulators in the EU ahead of the plans to begin running services in 2030.

articles.title: 'Don't stuff it': Labor relishes One Nation super fight
articles.body: Anthony Albanese has capitalised on Pauline Hanson's claim that the superannuation system is broken. Labor has seized the opportunity to defend the system during Question Time, accusing right-wing parties of threatening to dismantle the three-decade-old compulsory superannuation scheme. Prime Minister Albanese stated that One Nation wants to damage Australians' future by undermining universal super. Five ministers addressed benefits of superannuation for women, workers, parents, and the economy. One Nation MP Barnaby Joyce proposed allowing access to superannuation for those at risk of homelessness, citing individuals living in cars. However, Nationals leader Matt Canavan questioned Hanson’s policy, noting it was not fully developed. Current rules allow early withdrawals for financial hardship or medical needs, with limits on repayments and interest. Tax office data shows 67,900 early super releases in 2024/25, totaling over $1.4 billion. The Super Members Council warned that weakening compulsory superannuation would reduce retirement savings, increase aged pension dependency, and raise future taxes. Deputy Opposition Leader Jane Hume emphasized homeownership as crucial for economic security in retirement, contrasting with Liberal colleague Andrew Bragg’s criticism of compulsory super as a policy failure. The debate over superannuation access emerged amid negotiations on legislation, including cuts to the National Disability Insurance Scheme and gambling regulations.

articles.title: Revolutionizing Bangkok Commute: Single Ticket Policy Caps Electric Rail Fares at $1.36 for 2027 Launch
articles.body: Thailand has announced its intention to implement a common-ticket policy for electric rail services in Bangkok and the surrounding provinces. This initiative, which is expected to commence next year, will cap fares at 45 baht (US$1.36) per journey to streamline the public transportation system. Additionally, an initial cost of no more than 17 baht will be instituted, which will not be re-imposed if travelers switch to another line, as stated by Deputy Transport Minister Siripong Angkasakulkiat at a recent official gathering. Unifying Public Transportation The aim of the new fare bracket is to render Bangkok’s disjointed urban rail network more user-friendly. At present, passengers are required to negotiate separate ticketing systems, fare structures, and payment methods when moving between lines. The current SkyTrain fares can amount to as much as 65 baht, depending on the route, as per the Bangkok Mass Transit System’s data. The common-ticket policy’s legal and administrative procedures are projected to be finalized by November 2026. System testing is set to commence in December, leading up to the introduction of the common-ticket measure on January 1, 2027. Growth of the BTS SkyTrain The BTS SkyTrain, which began operations in December 1999 as Bangkok’s premier mass-transit rail system, has seen substantial upgrades since its inception. The original core network has expanded significantly to include approximately 68 kilometers of lines and 60 stations. In the last year, the BTS SkyTrain noted a 5.6% increase in ridership from 2024, recording a total of 205.4 million journeys.

articles.title: AUKUS offers Australia a nuclear solution to climate change
articles.body: There is something faintly old-fashioned about the climate debate. It remains obsessed with solar panels, public transport, building upgrades, electrification, and the tedious business of not cooking the planet. It assumes that a climate policy should preserve a liveable society, a benign climate, and keep food growing. Whilst charming, this is insufficiently ambitious. Australia is, after all, a nation capable of thinking strategically. We have learned to pronounce ‘cohesiveness’ and to discuss security in the commanding grammar of inevitability. So, when the Government tells us that climate disruption is an existential threat, while preparing substantial military infrastructure, perhaps the public should ask whether there is an ingenious solution. The Department of Defence says that, from as early as 2027, the planned Submarine Rotational Force at HMAS Stirling will involve one United Kingdom and up to four United States nuclear-powered submarines. Nuclear-powered submarines are not nuclear weapons, but U.S. and UK nuclear submarines do carry nuclear weapons, making them a target when docked in port—vulnerable as any sitting duck and a major concern for all residents. A leaked Cabinet Submission suggests a proposal to replace reducing emissions with a period of planetary dimming, followed by food-system collapse, ecological disruption, radioactive contamination, mass displacement, and an acute shortage of essentials. The key performance indicator is technically lowering temperatures for as long as anyone can record them. This proposal is praised for its fiscal discipline, as it avoids spending on improving homes against heat, building resilient public transport, restoring ecosystems, supporting Pacific climate adaptation, or rapidly replacing fossil fuels. The absurdity lies not in the idea of a nuclear-winter climate policy but in the policy that makes this joke intelligible. The real question is: What sort of future is being built? articles.title: Aggies Take Hornets To Wire In 1-0 Loss
articles.body: DAVIS, Calif. — UC Davis (1-1-0) took Sacramento State (2-0-0) down to the wire before falling, 1-0, in its home opener at Aggie Soccer Field on Sunday evening. The Aggies had a pair of scoring chances while trailing 1-0 in the 84th minute, but shots from Savannah Cordero and Ashley Brewer were off the right post and just left of the goal. Sacramento State's Ellie Farber scored the game's only goal on a penalty kick after being fouled by UC Davis' Stella Villalta in the penalty box. The match ended with nearly identical shooting statistics: Sacramento State held a 9-8 advantage in shots, while both teams put four on goal. Courtney Wagner had match-high three shots for the Aggies, and Raegan Rossi and Lexi Schroeder each had two shots on goal for Sacramento State. Delaney Timmons saved all four Aggie shots, and Dina Frenkel saved all three non-penalty shots. Sacramento State had a 7-3 advantage in corner kicks, while UC Davis committed almost twice as many fouls (11-6). UC Davis will continue its season with a nonconference match at Saint Mary's on Thursday, followed by a road game at Santa Clara on August 27 and a home game against UC Santa Barbara on August 30. The Aggies' first loss since 2017 ended their three-match home unbeaten streak. UC Davis Athletics, ranked No. 2 among public universities by the Wall Street Journal for the value of a college degree, is home to 40,000 undergraduates and 12,000 employees. The university is known for its excellence in agriculture, forestry, and veterinary medicine, located in a college town near major California destinations like the San Francisco Bay Area, Napa Valley, and Lake Tahoe. The Aggies compete in 25 Division I sports, with 16 transitioning to the Mountain West Conference starting in 2026–27.

articles.title: Skintown review – Northern Irish scamps rave their Troubles away
articles.body: D erry Girls meets Human Traffic in this spirited, larky and at times poignant period piece about raving and drug dealing scamps in Northern Ireland in the 1990s. It doesn’t suggest that the social revolution MDMA engendered in youth culture and spread to the rest of the UK in that decade played a causal role in the Northern Irish peace process. However, it notes the coincidence of the timing. The film’s centerpiece is a club night and beachside afterparty where Carl Cox DJs, with Catholics and Protestants coming together to dance, all juiced up on vitamin E, on the same day in August 1994 that the IRA announced an end to hostilities. At the afterparty, Catholic scamps from Enniskillen—known as Skintown—get involved with a British soldier, and their troubles seem to melt away. One character declares, ‘I love Brits. I love the IRA. I love the RUC. If you love them, you defuse them, they have no reason to fight you.’ The film and historical records show that while the mood was defiant apoliticism, the 1994 ceasefire was provisional. The protagonist Vinny, traumatized but seeking a fresh start, has an escape fund hidden in a biscuit tin. Vinny and his friend Jonty steal 400 pills from the Ulster Volunteer Force and sell them in a club, despite the presence of paramilitary thugs. Ciarán McMenamin adapted his own 2018 novel, incorporating many voiceover elements, which slightly detracts from immersion. However, the film includes vivid details, such as Jonty jokingly calling an ecstasy tablet ‘body of Christ’ and a wheelchair-bound raver dancing despite being paralyzed from the waist down by an IRA bullet. The club, Kellys in Portrush, County Antrim, was a utopian haven for dancers, and Carl Cox did play there in 1994. The soundtrack features Prodigy, Josh Wink, Jaydee, and Debussy choral pieces, enhancing the film’s nostalgic hedonism. While some may critique minor authenticity lapses, many viewers will appreciate the film’s portrayal of youthful rebellion and freedom.

articles.body: Mollie Gallagher found it 'so hard' saying goodbye to Coronation Street but knew it would be 'devastating' to pass up the chance to appear on stage. Mollie Gallagher was sad to leave her 'dream' job on Coronation Street after more than six years playing Nina Lucas because she realized her dream of juggling the role with playing Clarice Starling in a new UK theatre tour of The Silence of the Lambs could not work. She told Radio Times: "Originally I really wanted to find a way to do both. It sounds ridiculous hearing it now, but I'd seen theatre runs where different actors take on different stints, but I realized pretty quickly that could never work." It's so hard, because obviously being on Corrie has been her dream, but also she wants to explore other things. She was offered something as great as this, and not being able to do it would be devastating. Mollie has just begun her role in Silence of the Lambs, which runs until June 2027, and admitted she has been very nervous about stepping out on stage. She said: "This is only my second professional job! So I don't know if this ever goes away for anybody, but there is a big feeling of imposter syndrome." She feels like she's in the unknown, and unlike TV, you can't watch yourself back. But she has enjoyed the challenge of playing Clarice Starling, who must be grounded and not airy-fairy. She started practicing lines and realized she could do it. Meanwhile, the soap star hinted the door is left open for Nina to return in the future. She teased on This Morning: "I believed it's not the end of Nina's story. I love Corrie, and I really hope it's not the end." Last month, Corrie bosses voiced their support for Mollie's decision. A show spokesperson confirmed: "Mollie has created a unique and well-loved character in Nina over the past six and a half years and everyone will be sorry to see her go. Whenever I am asked who my favourite current cricketer is, I struggle to look beyond Root. He is such a grounded individual and clearly a fabulous player. He is also his own best coach, always first in the nets and last out of them, forever thinking about his game and how to improve those one-percenters. He has a wonderful sense of humour, and in his second spell as captain, my hope is that he can have more fun in the role, see the bigger picture, and not get bogged down by it. Playing under Ben Stokes should have taught him that. As badly as the whole thing ended, the better aspects of the environment under Stokes and Brendon McCullum are worth persevering with. Clearly, things are very different now. In his previous stint, Root was blessed with Jimmy Anderson and Stuart Broad at his disposal, but this stymied the development of other bowlers and limited his intuitive approach. He often felt one over behind the game rather than ahead. The appointment of Stephen Fleming as England’s Test head coach raises questions about their potential blend. Fleming, a former Test captain himself, is expected to challenge Root and broaden the leadership in the dressing room. Fleming’s approach, similar to Trevor Bayliss’s, is to be more in the background, allowing players with strong minds to lead. However, some on the sidelines believe Root and Alastair Cook needed a more proactive coach. Fleming’s arrival will hopefully encourage Root to trust his instincts and think outside the box. England’s current squad reflects a mix of bowlers with high potential but still finding their way. Roles are still being defined, and spots are yet to be fully locked down. articles.title: Swedish Krona: Riksbank steady as currency lags – BNY
articles.body: BNY's Wee Khoon Chong note Sweden’s Riksbank appears comfortable with its current policy stance as inflation stays below target, leaving two hikes in the repo path mainly as a risk acknowledgment. Despite favorable real-rate dynamics, Swedish Krona (SEK) performance is constrained by valuation concerns and a high KIX level. Chong expects the Riksbank to avoid aggressive SEK-supportive action while CPI remains anchored. Riksbank comfortable despite weak krona "We believe Sweden’s Riksbank – along with the Swiss National Bank – is the most “at ease” with its current policy path as inflation remains well below target levels." "Given the favorable outlook on prices and real rates , SEK performance might leave much to be desired." "The KIX, Sweden’s import-weighted exchange rate index, remains at the upper end of its recent range, which would normally prompt the Riksbank to state that the currency is undervalued." "The June Monetary Policy Report envisaged the KIX at an annualized average of 116.18, which is already an adjustment to reflect a weaker SEK (i.e., import prices go up)." "Swedish producer prices are clearly moving in tandem, but as long as CPI is anchored, we expect the Riksbank to hold off on being more assertive by bringing forward the two hikes currently in the repo path."
